blurb: Branches as names and heads. Reading history moved to commit.
reasons: Why one commit per row: today each row carries three full references (~550 B).
Why merge <branch> <from>: read as "into agent, from main", like git merge on a checked-out Branch. --into writes the result to a new Branch instead, which is the only form the code has today.
Why --expected on publish guards main: publish writes main. The Commit to publish is named with --at, so the Branch moving cannot change what is published.
Why the prefix filters: the UI fetches every Branch, then drops the internal dsh.* ones.

calls.note: one commit replaces head/saved_head/base: the Branch's head, or the Commit it was forked at while it has none of its own; main is a row, and its commit is main's head; forked_from (long form) is the Commit the Branch was forked at, not a Branch name: the record keeps the Commit; no created_at: a Branch record has no time; a cursor carries the call's filters only, and pins no Commit: given with other filters, or to another call, it is refused InvalidInput
calls.help: a project's Branches, main included, in name order
calls.cli: layerfs branch list <project> [--prefix P] [--exclude-prefix P] [--limit 100] [--cursor C]

options.name: prefix
options.help: only Branches whose name starts with this text

options.name: exclude_prefix
options.help: leave out Branches whose name starts with this text, such as dsh.

options.name: limit
options.help: the most rows in one page, 1 to 1000

options.name: cursor
options.help: the `next_cursor` of the page before; it carries the filters only

calls.new_work: `--prefix` and `--exclude-prefix` are new: today only a folder scope filters Branches, by its namespace, on the caller's side after reading every page. `--cursor` is new: today the call pages by position (`page_size`, `page_pos`, default 50). The cursor carries the call's filters only, and no Commit; one given with other filters, or to another call, is refused `InvalidInput`.

calls.note: the head to pass as --expected; forked_from (long form) is the Commit the Branch was forked at
calls.help: one Branch and its head Commit

calls.note: from defaults to main; --at forks at a Commit instead of that Branch's head; commit is the Commit the new Branch starts at
calls.help: a new Branch from another Branch's head, or from a Commit

options.name: at
options.help: fork at this Commit instead of the head of `from`: a full id, or a prefix of 8 or more characters

dropped.why: optional now; main when left off
one way to name a Commit

calls.new_work: An id prefix is new: today the call takes a full 66-character id. A prefix that matches more than one Commit is refused `InvalidInput` with `matches`, a count.

calls.note: merges from into branch; --into NEW writes the result to a new Branch and changes neither, as today; rules come from branch's /.lww; --units is kept; --expected guards branch's head in both forms; a conflict is the refusal Conflict, which lists the conflicts and changes nothing; fast_forward when one side held the other and no Commit was made; overwritten lists the paths a newer-write-wins rule decided; parent and second_parent are the two heads merged
calls.help: merge one Branch into another, or into a new Branch
calls.cli: layerfs branch merge <project> <branch> <from> [--into NEW] [--units JSON] [--expected C] [-m msg]

options.name: into
options.help: write the result to a new Branch of this name and leave `branch` as it is

options.name: units
options.help: merge units: a list of patterns or {name, patterns}; a unit both sides changed is taken whole from the side with the later write

options.name: expected
options.help: refuse `Conflict` unless `branch`'s head is this Commit

options.name: message
options.help: the merge Commit's message; `-m` in the shell; `Merge <branch> and <from>` when left off

dropped.why: the new Branch is optional now
the Branch merged into; its rules apply

calls.new_work: Merging into an existing Branch is new: today `branch.merge` always makes a new Branch (`--into NEW` is that form) and never changes either side. Moving `branch`'s head to the merge result, `--expected`, and `unchanged` (when `branch` already holds `from`) are part of that work. An id prefix for `--expected` is new. A prefix that matches more than one Commit is refused `InvalidInput` with `matches`, a count.

calls.note: commit is main's new head; --expected guards main's head (today's expected_base); naming the Commit with --at replaces expected_head; adds unchanged:true when main already holds it, or previous (main's head before) when that was not the Branch's base; the Layers a forced publication replaced are the rows commit list <project> main shows between the new head and base
calls.help: a Branch's head or Commit as main's next head, refusing a stale base

options.name: at
options.help: publish this Commit instead of the Branch's head: a full id, or a prefix of 8 or more characters

options.name: expected
options.help: refuse `Conflict` unless main's head is this Commit

options.name: force
options.help: publish over what main gained since the Branch forked

the one write guard; it guards main's head
naming the Commit to publish pins what is published; a moved Branch head cannot change it

calls.new_work: An id prefix is new: today the call takes a full 66-character id. A prefix that matches more than one Commit is refused `InvalidInput` with `matches`, a count. The refusal of a stale `--expected` is `Conflict` and names main's head as `commit` (`HeadMoved` today).
